title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Iran: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Iran: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Iran: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Preparing legal, medical, and financial arrangements in advance for someone facing serious or terminal illness in Iran involves coordinating Iranian Civil Code agency rules, tax filings, social insurance benefits, and consular procedures [3][5][6]. Because several domestic Iranian government websites (including the Ministry of Health, Legal Medicine Organization, parliamentary statutory databases, and certain Social Security Organization PDF servers) restrict external HTTPS requests or lack accessible English administrative workflows from abroad, this guide relies on reachable civil-registration and consular portals alongside verified international legal repositories (WIPO Lex, FAOLEX, and ILO NATLEX) and foreign civil-document reciprocity schedules, advising direct verification in person with local Iranian offices or accredited consulates [1][2][3][6][9].

steps.title: Healthcare documentation, consent, and welfare assessments
steps.html:
• Medical records and hospital consent practice: Public, university, and private hospitals in Iran do not operate a uniform statutory advance-directive registry; documenting treatment wishes with the attending medical team and identifying one primary family spokesperson helps streamline consent discussions during inpatient care [3].
  • Disability and rehabilitation medical commissions: Under the Comprehensive Law on Disability Rights, patients with severe functional limitations should arrange formal evaluation before a Medical Committee of the State Welfare Organization of Iran (Behzisti Medical Committees) to qualify for rehabilitation support, home-care subsidies, and municipal accessibility services [7].
  • Organizing identity records for care: Keeping valid copies of the patient's National ID Card (Kart-e Melli), identity booklet (Shenasnameh), and health insurance booklet together accelerates hospital admission and later civil notifications with the National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval) [2][9].

steps.title: Powers of attorney (Vikalatnama), Mikhak, and capacity limits
steps.html:
• Domestic notarial execution: Within Iran, granting authority to manage bank accounts, pension filings, or property matters requires executing an official Power of Attorney (Vikalatnama) before Notary Public Offices (Daftar-e Asnad-e Rasmi) and Public Courts while the principal has full legal capacity [3].
  • Consular Mikhak system from abroad: Principals or family members residing outside Iran initiate Powers of Attorney online through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Mikhak Consular Power of Attorney Service), obtain a tracking code, and attend the relevant Iranian diplomatic mission or interests section in person with a valid passport, Shenasnameh, or National ID Card for signature verification [2][8].
  • Automatic termination rules: Under Iranian civil-law agency provisions in the Civil Code of the Islamic Republic of Iran, a Vikalatnama remains effective only while the principal retains mental capacity and automatically terminates upon judicial interdiction or death, so early notarization is critical [3][4].

steps.title: Iranian Civil Code wills, succession structure, and tax preparation
steps.html:
• Statutory inheritance vs. testamentary freedom: Succession in Iran is governed by the Civil Code of the Islamic Republic of Iran (Articles 825 and 906 to 915), establishing fixed Islamic shares by kinship class (for example, sons receiving twice the share of daughters under Article 907, and differentiated spousal shares under Article 913), alongside recognized minority personal-status rules; a will (Vasiyat) may freely allocate up to one-third of the net estate, whereas any disposition beyond one-third requires consent of the other heirs [3][4].
  • Inheritance tax readiness under the Direct Taxation Act: Organizing bank statements, property title deeds (Sanad), unpaid marriage-portion (Mahr) records, and verified debt documentation helps future heirs submit timely tax returns and claim deductions and pension or life-insurance exemptions under Chapter 4 (Articles 17 to 24) of the Direct Taxation Act [5].
  • Cross-border estate inventories: Because Iran taxes or assesses estate assets located in Iran even for non-resident Iranian nationals and foreign heirs (Article 17), maintaining bilingual asset lists prevents delays in securing the court Certificate of Inheritance later on [2][5].

steps.title: Social security disability benefits and caregiving leave
steps.html:
• Social Security Organization disability and care coverage: Insured employees should confirm contribution histories with the Social Security Organization of Iran (Tamin Ejtema'i) under the 1975 Social Security Law, which governs medical treatment, sickness benefits, permanent or partial disability pensions, and future survivor entitlements [6].
  • Welfare subsidies and tax exemptions for dependents: Dependent heirs with certified disabilities qualify for expanded tax-exempt thresholds under Article 20 of the Direct Taxation Act alongside support coordinated by the State Welfare Organization of Iran (Behzisti Medical Committees) [5][7].
  • Workplace medical leave coordination: Ensuring attending physicians issue stamped medical-commission certificates protects ongoing sickness-benefit payments and prevents gaps in social insurance contributions during prolonged illness [6].

steps.title: Civil-registry accuracy and non-Apostille consular legalization
steps.html:
• Updating Sabte Ahval civil entries: Verifying accurate spelling across the patient's Shenasnameh, Kart-e Melli, and foreign passports with the National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval) reduces downstream discrepancies when foreign or domestic documents are paired later [1][2][9].
  • No Apostille recognition: According to the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH) status table, Iran is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; an Apostille certificate cannot be used to validate documents entering or leaving Iran [10].
  • Sequential consular legalization: Foreign medical reports, bilingual powers of attorney, and civil certificates destined for Iranian banks, courts, or ministries must complete consular legalization through the issuing country's foreign ministry and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Mikhak Consular Power of Attorney Service) or designated interests section [1][2][8][10].

closingQuestion: Are you organizing a Vikalatnama and care support inside Iran, or preparing cross-border authorizations through the Mikhak consular portal?

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran (Mikhak Consular Power of Attorney Service)
contacts.note: Online Mikhak intake and consular verification service authenticating Vikalatnama powers of attorney and foreign civil/medical records.

contacts.name: State Welfare Organization of Iran (Behzisti Medical Committees)
contacts.note: Conducts medical disability assessments and coordinates rehabilitation, assistive care, and caregiver support subsidies under Iran's Disability Rights Law.

contacts.name: Social Security Organization of Iran (Tamin Ejtema'i)
contacts.note: Administers sickness allowances, disability pensions, healthcare coverage, and survivor insurance benefits under the 1975 Social Security Law.

contacts.name: National Organization for Civil Registration (Sabte Ahval)
contacts.note: Maintains national identity cards (Kart-e Melli), Shenasnameh booklets, and vital event records in Iran.

contacts.name: Notary Public Offices (Daftar-e Asnad-e Rasmi) and Public Courts
contacts.note: Authenticate domestic wills, powers of attorney, and property records and oversee future inheritance proceedings under the Civil Code.
